lesson_title: Dots, Dashes and a Ringing Bell
hook_text: The first messages sent by electricity were not words at all. They were dots and dashes.
clip_script: A telegraph office long ago. An operator taps a brass key: short, short, long. Dots and dashes race along a wire on tall poles, across the country, in seconds. At the other end, another operator writes down the message, and a boy on a bicycle rushes the telegram to a house. Then a new sound: a bell rings, someone lifts a heavy black handset and says hello, and hears a voice from far away. Messages by wire changed the world.
visual_style: Whiteboard telegraph key sending dots and dashes along a wire on poles to a receiving office, a messenger on a bicycle, then an old telephone, an operator at a switchboard and a phone line to a house.
mood: Exciting and inventive, like cracking a secret code.
pacing: Tap-tap rhythm for the telegraph, then a ring and a pause before the first hello.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and tap out your name in Morse code.
